project_announced_description: This USDA Rural Development investment will be used to rebuild and update the deteriorating facade of the covered main and emergency department entries of the Northern Cochise Community Hospital, a critical emergency and trauma center in northeast Cochise County. The overhead canopies are approximately 50 years old, too low, and do not accommodate current vehicle sizes; and periodically vehicles collide into the canopies and/or into the cement bollards that protect the canopy support structure. Structural upgrades will be made to the canopies that are under-protected against vehicle impacts, and the current bollards are almost pushed back against the single support post on the emergency department canopy. As a result of collisions, the protective concrete curbing is cracked and denigrated. A vehicle hit can cause the canopy to collapse and cause property damage and serious harm to people. Also, the current roof water drainage is causing damage to the building's exterior brick and grounds. This facade update will provide proper roof water drainage to protect the exterior roofing overhang soffits and the building's exterior.

The project is expected to save eight jobs during the project period and an additional 10 jobs through 2025.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used by a nonprofit community organization to provide small business and financial literacy and long-term business strategic planning training for Navajo Nation communities and their leadership. Dine Community Development Corporation will also use project funds to develop a Navajo hemp production feasibility study and business plan to determine the viability of the hemp business concept, such as ensuring the legal and technical feasibility and economic justification. The study will encompass the proposal of an industrial hemp production facility on the Navajo Nation as well as the creation of a Commission to oversee all hemp operations within the reservation. A business plan will then be developed from the results of the feasibility study for a viable hemp business opportunity. These projects will address the Navajo Nations high unemployment rate while increasing local economic development activities. The project is expected to save seven and create fourteen jobs.

funding_code: SMALL SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED PRODUCER GRANT
naics_industry_sector: Other Services
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to develop a Navajo Financial Cooperative program for the Navajo Nation and surrounding tribal communities. The proposed Navajo Financial Cooperative Feasibility Study and Business Plan will be used to develop a reservation-based financial/credit union cooperative program where a Din/Native American-owned financial institution can help combat credit deserts in rural and Indigenous areas. The Navajo Nation lacks access to financial entities, and the surrounding rural communities as well; and financial cooperatives and credit unions help strengthen the economy and empower people with ownership over their financial institution. The objective of establishing a Navajo Financial Cooperative is to develop a reservation-based credit union such as a type of financial institution similar to a commercial bank that will be a Navajo member-owned financial cooperative, controlled by its Navajo/Native American members and operated on a not-for-profit basis. The financial/credit union coop will provide services to members similar to retail banks, including deposit accounts, provision of credit, and other financial services that is currently lacking on the reservation.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist member tribes in effectively managing and mitigating solid waste to protect the environment on tribal lands and the health of American Indians. Inter Tribal Council of Arizona will conduct trainings for tribal members and tribal solid waste personnel on specific landfill issues, stormwater management, large vehicle management, birds and other vectors, and litter mitigation, diversion rates in the United States, Occupational Safety and Health Administration safety pertaining to landfill and transfer station workers, Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response refresher course, and composting.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used toprovide its technical assistance, training, and tribal operator certification services to small, rural tribal communities located in USEPA Regions 5 through 10-a project service area spanning 28 states and 96 percent of all tribal public water systems in the U.S. The following four project activities will be implemented. First, ITCA will strengthen tribal water utility resilience by providing resiliency technical assistance (TA) and conducting resiliency training. Second, ITCA will strengthen tribal utility managerial and financial (M&F) capacity by providing M&F-TA, conducting Tribal Utility Tune-Up (EUM "workshop in a box")Workshops, and conducting training-Tribal Utility Management Certification training, as well as training on utility finance, asset management, and water loss control. Third, ITCA will strengthen tribal utility operations & maintenance (O&M) capacity by providing O&M-TA, conducting operator fundamentals trainings and free regional tribal operator certification training events, offering travel reimbursement stipends, and creating a new type of tribal operator certification for tribal wastewater lagoon operators. In addition, ITCA will improve the workforce pipeline by exploring potentials for developing workforce pipeline linkages with tribal colleges and universities. Fourth, ITCA will improve tribal water utility capacity for complying with federal regulations by conducting federal regulations training events.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to partially fund an Anaerobic Digester facility located on the Butterfield Dairy near Gila Bend, Arizona. The digester will convert cow manure into renewable natural gas (RNG) to be inserted into a nearby pipeline and ultimately used for transportation fuel in California, earning Low Carbon Fuel Standards (LCFS) credits in addition to the revenue from the sale of the RNG. The facility will generate 90,111,079 kWh of energy per year, or the equivalent of 8,462 US homes. The project is also expected to generate revenues in excess of $24 million annually, a portion of which will remain in the local community.

funding_code: (COMB LOAN & GRANT) WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase the existing Aguila Water Service water system, which consists of two wells, three steel water storage tanks (one inactive), two booster stations with hydro-pneumatic tanks (one booster has two 5,000 gallon hydro-pneumatic tanks and the other has one small hydro tank), two standpipes with distribution meters, and 16.3 miles of distribution system pipeline, ranging in size from 4-inches to 6-inches. Minor improvements will also be made to the system consisting of upgrades to the pump and piping coating system, new service flow control valve, purchase of 330 new drive-by radio water meters with installation of 319, which will be supported by meter reading/accounting equipment. The water system will also purchase a new 60k watt emergency stand-by generator and associated electrical improvements made, and purchase a truck to be used to collect usage data from the new drive-by radio water meters. This project will promote system efficiency to avoid seeking additional water sources, promote water conservation, and continue to provide reliable local service for the community of Aguila, Arizona, an unincorporated area in Maricopa County.

funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) 306C  WATER ONLY (COLONIAS)
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to rehabilitate one existing well, replace existing well pump, replace existing above ground piping, including valves, replace existing electrical panels and well control panels; rehabilitate existing storage tanks and replace the pumps and associated equipment; replace the two existing booster pumps, replace the above ground piping, check valves, gate valves, and restrained couplings; replace existing hydro pneumatic tank; replace meters; make improvements to the filtration plant; and most recently, replace well #4, as it has failed. The Town of Kearny operates a public water system located within Pinal County, Arizona, and a population of 1,882 is served by the water system. The water system consists of four wells, two steel water storage tanks, one booster station with a hydro pneumatic tank, a water treatment plant (Filtration Plant), and 10.3 miles of distribution pipeline. The water meters are over 20 years old and water loss is shown at 27%. The proposed improvements are related to aging infrastructure that are at the end of useful life, and do not satisfy a health or sanitary concern. The town needs water infrastructure improvements to continue to supply potable water to its customers. The rehabilitation and replacements made to the water system will increase system efficiency to avoid seeking additional water sources, promote water conservation, and provide reliable service.

funding_code: NATIVE AMERICAN TRIBES COMMUNITY FACILITY GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Educational Services
naics_national_industry: ALL OTHER MISCELLANEOUS SCHOOLS AND INSTRUCTION
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide infrastructure development at the Dine College Tsaile and Shiprock Campus Demonstration Farms supporting formal and informal education for students and community members pursuing agriculture careers or current farmers and ranchers. Both facilities will be used for training, seminars, workshops and educational courses that are essential in agriculture programs. At the Tsaile Campus, funds will be used to remove old electrical units, identify utility sources, and prepare the land for the new facility to be built. The building will incorporate classrooms and indoor livestock working facilities, a temporary holding facility for livestock, indoor space to conduct presentations, and a birthing area. At the Shiprock Campus, funds will be used to restore the sediment pond, install an irrigation pump station, install irrigation pipelines and valves, construct drainage ditches, construct perimeter fencing, land leveling, and site utilities. The construction of the Shiprock Agriculture Multipurpose Center will house classrooms, training space, and a commercial kitchen allowing farmers to wash, prepare, and store their produce. It will serve as the headquarters of the Business Center for Training in Horticulture and Tribal Agriculture. Training provided at the two campuses will help produce healthy, quality livestock and products for Navajo Farmers.
